title: Overdispersed and zero-inflated counts transported by G-computation
question: For count outcomes transported to a target, does overdispersion bias the estimate or only its interval, and when the fraction of structural zeros differs between populations, what does a count model transport wrongly and what repairs it?
design: G-computation from an individual-data trial with negative-binomial or zero-inflated Poisson counts, 14 cells separating dispersion from structural-zero differences, with and without effect modification; Poisson, sandwich, negative binomial, zero-inflated and recalibrated zero-inflated fits. 500 replicates per cell.
